title: Design: Closed internal work order shows the INTERNAL document
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin (a user with every setting, See Financial Data included).
  • Use a desktop browser window 1440 pixels wide at 100% zoom.
  • Have Internal Work Orders turned on in Settings > Work Orders.
  • Use a location that is connected to QuickBooks Online, with every ShopView Accounts row mapped.
  • Have a customer flagged as Internal customer, with one asset, and its default internal category left at General Internal.
  • Have a closed internal work order with stock parts, 3.0 h of labor and shop supplies $25.00, made for this test.
  • Open the attached pictures iwo-flow1-22-08-work-order-closed-invoice.png, iwo-happy-18-18-closed-internal-document.png at 100% zoom beside the screen.
custom_steps:
1. Open the closed internal work order.
  2. Click the Finance tab.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • The header shows the status Closed with the Internal badge and the line "Closed on [posting date]. To change it, reopen it from the Finance tab."; no Reopen button.

Step 2:

  • The document's masthead shows the letterhead left, the shop logo in the centre and "Internal Work Order [number]" with the date on the right.
  • Under the masthead, on the left and never over the logo, the INTERNAL stamp with "Category: General Internal".
  • Labor lines with hours only, parts with quantity and cost only, and a Summary with Parts cost, Shop supplies $25.00 and Labor hours; no tax, total, payments, balance or signature.
  • Download, Print and Email are offered.

Words in square brackets in a message stand for the value they name, such as the work order's number or the customer's name exactly as it is saved; every other word of the message must match exactly.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Internal Work Orders (PRD)", Confluence 942243841, version 1.0 final (9 Nov 2026, Milos Vasic), read 12 Nov 2026 · Epic SV-11665, story SV-11760 (Story 3, Close an internal or no-charge work order), story SV-11767 (Story 10, Shop supplies on internal and no-charge work orders)

  • S3-R5: “The Finance tab of a closed work order shows the NO CHARGE document: the masthead as on the invoice today (letterhead left, the shop logo in the centre slot, the document block "Internal Work Order [number]" or "No Charge Work Order [number]" with the date right), and under the masthead line, on the left and never over the logo, the INTERNAL or NO CHARGE stamp with the line "Category: [name]" and, when set, "· Original work order [number]" (a link in ShopView, plain on the PDF), Bill to the customer, the asset block, labor lines with hours only, parts lines with quantity and cost only (cost under 'See Financial Data'), a Summary with Parts cost (one number: stock parts plus special orders and sublet, at the amounts of S3-R2, core cost excluded, S2-E7), Shop supplies (when above $0.00) and Labor hours (the labor hours on the lines), and no tax, total, payments, balance or signature block; with Download, Print and Email (the recipient field is empty; the user types the shop's own address or any other; never automatically). The Customer PO field is not required. The internal invoice carries the work order number, as every invoice does today; no number is consumed or skipped. Parts cost on the document and in the report is fixed at Close: a vendor bill entered, edited or deleted after Close posts its own amounts to the work order's expense account (S7-R3) and changes neither the document nor the report. Email uses the invoice email template of today (it carries no amounts) with the subject "Internal Work Order [number]" or "No Charge Work Order [number]".”
  • S2-R9: “From Close or invoice on, the classification and the category are locked: a closed no-charge work order shows the No Charge badge with no Convert or Change category action, on a closed internal or no-charge work order the Change Customer button on the customer card is disabled with the tooltip "Reopen the work order to change the customer." (the lock an invoiced or paid billable work order has today, S2-R7), and the header card carries the line "Closed on [posting date]. To change it, reopen it from the Finance tab."”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.

References from Design

Design canvas "Internal Work Orders · All flows v6" (https://claude.ai/artifact/5jHR3nLeDinzks1viREFuo), version 1794484794-2031, read and rendered 12 Nov 2026: pages "Flow 1 · Create and close" / "Happy flow v6", boards "08 Work order · Closed, invoice" (Flow 1 · Create and close), "18 Closed · INTERNAL document" (Happy flow v6).

Design pictures attached to this case:

  • iwo-flow1-22-08-work-order-closed-invoice.png
  • iwo-happy-18-18-closed-internal-document.png

The design's own words:

  • “INTERNAL”
  • “Category: General Internal”
  • “Parts cost”
  • “Shop supplies”

Difference: the design adds a Reopen button in the header (IWO-D27), prints "Labor" for Labor hours (IWO-D32) and draws the alert without an X (IWO-D28), settled by S4-R1, S3-R5 and S3-EH.
